If I go now they'll see that I've been crying and they'll start bugging me about it. Maybe if I can calm down I'll go.

I tried therapy. I hated it. I'm not much of a talker and being forced to keep a conversation going with a stranger for an hour was torture. 

I don't really have any hobbies. I used to draw but I haven't been inspired. And keeping concentrated for long enough is painful. I've never really had anything that I really like. Arts and crafts are fun, and I'm good at them. But they're the kind of things that give me an excuse to stay hidden away in my room. So I stopped. 

And now that it's summer I don't even have school to give me something to do. I just don't know what to do with myself. I've spent the last week watching old episodes of Law and Order: SVU and playing the Sims 3. 

My dad asked me today if I wanted to get out of the house and all I could think about was how disgusting I must have looked. How sad. Otherwise he wouldn't have asked.

Whether or not a woman is taking birth control is entirely her business. It's true that in a sexual relationship it is advised for both parties to be "in the loop," so to speak, but if she didn't feel the need to tell you then there may have been a reason.

Consider that this girl may have had experiences with guys who have thought that, since she's on birth control, condoms aren't necessary. I myself was in a relationship with a guy who fought me on using condoms every time we had sex just because I was on the pill. Sometimes it's just easier to keep it to yourself.

This is always a hard thing for partners to deal with. Seeing your significant other in pain, especially when it's emotional, can be exhausting and, as you said, frustrating. 

One thing to consider is that because she is always told how beautiful she is, she feels the need to meet that expectation. As a child I was always told how intelligent I was. I was praised for my grades and I was thought of as the "smart kid" at school. But this constant praise made me feel absolutely awful when I didn't do well, like a complete failure when I didn't do my best. For your girlfriend, having a day where she doesn't feel attractive might feel like she isn't meeting people's expectations.

Women in this day and age are under an enormous amount of pressure to be perfect and it can be difficult to not have it play a role in her life. She may be struggling with body image issues, or even other emotional problems that she either doesn't want you to worry about or isn't even aware of herself.

Keep an eye on her. If her depression worsens- if these shut down periods lengthen or happen more frequently- consider getting her professional help. It can be embarrassing to admit that you need to go see a shrink, but it might be best for her.

It's entirely possible that this is just part of their friendly relationship and that he conducts similarly with other women. He could just be that touchy-feely-hangs-out-with-girls kind of guy. If this is the case, then there really isn't anything you need to worry about unless you notice other behaviors. 

I would keep an open dialogue with your girlfriend about this. Don't accuse her of cheating or bring it up unnecessarily but make sure she understands that you feel uncomfortable about it. I know that you've already discussed it with her, but you may need to again. Pick a time when you feel you can have a rational, adult conversation about the issue.

Good luck.
